fig:bias-cells.old: Fake-data bias of the reported five-observable estimator on the sixteen cells, at the twelve graded truths of table~\ref{tab:fd16}, in the same order. Color gives the signed residual $z$, the mean fractional residual, (unfolded $-$ true)/true, divided by its uncertainty $\sqrt{\mathrm{diag}(C+N)}$, where $N$ is the noise covariance of that mean. The noise-free closure uses its single residual and $N=0$. Left panel: the reported covariance, $C_{\mathrm{total}}+C_{\mathrm{resp}}+C_{\mathrm{PL,5D}}$. Right panel: the covariance without the run-period block. The table's $C_{\mathrm{total}}$-only reading is not shown. Each covariance omits the truth's own generator component as in the table. Numbers give the largest $|z|$ in each outlined row, to two decimals; in the left panel they are those of table~\ref{tab:fd16}. Black outlines show only the per-cell criterion, $|z|>\fvval{trig-z}$. A truth can also be flagged by its $\chi^2$ $p$ value (table~\ref{tab:fd16}), as the synthetic $q_3$ tilt is under the reported covariance. The bias is identical in both panels; only the covariance differs. An asterisk marks the simulation's own truth. These tests assess only bias.

fig:rounding-shifts.old: Rounding-level shifts of the reported five-observable estimator. The cumulative distribution shows, for each of the 153 quantities, the larger absolute shift under two rounding-level perturbations of the data, divided by the study's own data-bootstrap statistical standard deviation (100 refitted replicas; the reported statistical block uses 50, section~\ref{sec:cov5d}). The quantities are the 109 supported joint (J) cell integrals, all 42 $(E_{\mathrm{avail}},W)$ cells, including the three outside the support rule used in figure~\ref{fig:prior-response}, and two totals. The edge-safe perturbations hold values on an analysis-grid edge fixed and move other inputs by at most half a float32 unit in the last place; the reference is the unperturbed inputs in float64. Vertical lines mark the requirements fixed before the test: at most 0.3 statistical standard deviations for the median and 1.0 for the maximum. The observed median and largest shift are marked, at the text's precision. Points in this distribution are different quantities, not repeated experiments.

Points are different quantities, not repeated experiments.

fig:prior-response.old:
Sensitivity to the prior of the reported five-observable estimator at five iterations. The vertical axis gives the fractional change of the data result, using the reported estimator with its background refinement, when the simulation prior is reweighted to the NuWro $(p_T,p_\parallel,E_{\mathrm{avail}})$ shape. The horizontal axis is minus the noise-free residual, (unfolded $-$ true)/true, at that changed truth: this comparator uses signal-only simulation, with no background refinement, whereas the data result uses the reported estimator's background refinement. Panels (a), (b) and (c) use the joint (J, 109), coarser joint (H2, 27) and $(E_{\mathrm{avail}},W)$ (EW, 39) cells defined in the companion note (
sec{sec:gbdt-model-dependence}; 
app{sec:gbdt-diagnostic-definitions}); no panel is the sixteen-cell result. Points are cells, not independent repeated experiments. The dotted line is $y=x$, for reference, with no fit. The shifts measure sensitivity to the prior, not a measured bias of the data result. The correlation supplies no per-cell bias bound (
sec{sec:gbdt-model-dependence}).
